newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTO RETAIN LEAD, BENFICA CLOSE GAP ON SPORTING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTO RETAIN LEAD, BENFICA CLOSE GAP ON SPORTING.

text.p: Benfica beat Gil Vicente 1-0, ending a series of four games without a win, and came closer to rivals Sporting, who drew at Farense 0-0 in the battle for second place in the Portuguese championship on Saturday.
Porto retained their commanding lead after an easy 2-0 win over struggling Uniao Leiria at home.
Porto now have 53 points in the championship, followed by Sporting with 38 and Benfica with 37.
Benfica gave a lacklustre performance and their Swedish striker Martin Pringle scored the match's only goal 10 minutes from the end when Gil Vicente were down to 10 men.
Pringle shot into the net from close range after taking a long pass from midfielder Glenn Helder.
Gil Vicente's striker Carlitos Cunha was sent off in the 73rd minute after two bookable offences.

"Our players were poorly prepared physically, but I hope that the team will be in good shape when we meet the Italians of Fiorentina in the Cup Winner's Cup quarter-finals next month," said Benfica's new coach Manuel Jose, who replaced Brazilian Paulo Autuori a fortnight ago.
Porto had an easy task against Uniao Leiria who ended the match with nine players after the expulsion of defender Paulito Matias and striker Mario Tilico for bookable offences.

Midfielder Jose Barroso scored from a free kick three minutes before half time and Brazilian striker and league top scorer Mario Jardel struck in the 41st minute, raising his tally this season to 17 goals.
